So this afternoon we'd like to acknowledge one of our amazing members of our city clerk's office
who has achieved the AMCTO Executive Diploma and Municipal Management Equity Scholarship.
And we'd like to congratulate Mariah Blake on that.
Mariah, as we all know, is a municipal professional with over seven years of experience across local government, federal service, and the nonprofit sector.
She currently serves as one of our committee coordinators with the City of Kitchener,
where she supports governance, legislative processes, and public engagement to help foster transparent and effective decision making.
Throughout her career, Mariah has worked at the intersection of policy, community engagement,
and service delivery.
Her experience includes supporting the Minister of Diversity, Inclusion, and Youth at the
federal level, coordinating complex municipal initiatives, and working directly with community
members in frontline and non-profit environments.
This diverse background informs her collaborative approach and her commitment to connecting strategic
priorities with community needs.
Mariah is also passionate about local governments, advancing equity in the workplace, and building
strong communities from the ground up.
A lifelong learner, she's committed to inclusive, holistic public service and is proud to contribute
to resilient, connected communities through both her professional and volunteer work.
As this year's EDMM Equity Scholarship recipient, Mariah will be enrolled in the program beginning
this fall, where she'll develop further foundational knowledge, skills, and competencies required
to be a successful local government manager.
The program helps support those with three or more years
of supervisor experience, mid-level managers,
and high-level municipal employees on track
to take on senior management or leadership roles.
The EDMM Equity Scholarship is an annual program
that will accept applications from eligible individuals each spring
for enrollment in the subsequent fall program,
registration for EDMM, and other AMCTO education programs
for the upcoming fall 2026 term opens.
